| `REQ-001` | Equivalent prompt, file, and skill inputs retain the same objective, deliverables, acceptance criteria, constraints, source references, project root, and action-authority boundary., An upstream handoff retains any supplied document or plan ID and its inspected revision or digest. Merely opening or approving a document does not start execution. | `satisfied` | 2 | None |
| `REQ-002` | A native runtime receipt identifies the manager as an agent instance distinct from the calling host; relabeling the host does not satisfy the requirement., The calling host relays user input and results after handoff without concurrently performing the same manager responsibilities. Repeated intake for the same live execution does not create a competing manager. | `satisfied` | 2 | None |
| `REQ-003` | Before decomposition, its inspectable context identifies the owning project, relevant architecture and interfaces, state ownership, dependencies, constraints, protected behavior, change impact, risks, and verification needs., The applicable local guidance and relevant project artifacts support that context. The manager retains scope, role selection, coordination, acceptance, integration, and final verification responsibility. | `satisfied` | 2 | None |
| `REQ-004` | Each executable subtask identifies its objective, requirement links, inputs, dependencies, deliverable, accountable assignment, allowed reads and writes, protected scope, acceptance criteria, and stopping condition., Missing dependency targets and dependency cycles prevent dependent execution. A small objective may use one generic subtask; mixed-category tasks retain main-task integration checks. | `satisfied` | 2 | None |
| `REQ-005` | No runnable subtask is uncategorized or substitutes `direct`, `decomposed`, or `adversarial` for the required category. Decomposition and category selection remain separate decisions., Reclassification records the changed evidence and applicable gates. It cannot silently bypass failed review, reduce a required team because of capacity, or split an inseparable decision solely to evade review. | `satisfied` | 2 | None |
| `REQ-006` | One worker returns its deliverables, actual changes, proportionate checks, evidence, and limitations to the manager. The category adds no solver panel, reviewer agent, senior synthesizer, or separate implementation child., Targeted corrections return to the responsible worker. Replacement after failure records revocation of the previous ownership before assigning a replacement; the manager directly verifies the result. | `satisfied` | 2 | None |
| `REQ-007` | All planned solvers receive the same versioned problem baseline and success criteria, with documented role differences. Two is a minimum, not a fixed required team size., Initial candidate development excludes sibling drafts, including for queued solvers. Separate candidate artifacts identify each contribution; competing solvers do not implement conflicting production changes in the shared worktree., A missing required candidate blocks collection. A runtime that cannot preserve the required independence reports the limitation instead of claiming independent development. | `satisfied` | 3 | None |
| `REQ-008` | The senior is a distinct runtime instance from the manager and solvers; for extra-complex work it is also distinct from the assigned reviewers., The senior receives every required current candidate, relevant evidence, limitations, and applicable review findings. Complex work has no mandatory per-candidate reviewer stage; extra-complex eligibility follows REQ-014. | `satisfied` | 2 | None |
| `REQ-009` | The proposal identifies its current source candidates, retained contributions, justified omissions, resolved differences, assumptions, interfaces, requirement coverage, residual risks, and verification approach., The result contains no unresolved mutually exclusive core commitments. Concatenation, majority vote, an unexplained preferred candidate, or an unsupported endorsement does not satisfy fusion. | `satisfied` | 2 | None |
| `REQ-010` | The conflict identifies the synthesis round, common problem baseline, candidate versions, incompatible claims, affected requirements, supporting evidence, and required resolution., All solver assignments receive the same shared explanation; any role-specific action notes are separate. An opposing core commitment is not discarded merely to declare a winner. | `satisfied` | 2 | None |
| `REQ-011` | Affected originating solvers return materially revised candidates or resolving evidence. An unaffected solver may return a versioned revalidation explaining compatibility., The next synthesis uses a consistent current candidate set and problem baseline. Repeated unchanged failure or exhausted authorized resources produces an honest non-complete state, never forced acceptance. | `satisfied` | 2 | None |
| `REQ-012` | The solver-to-reviewer mapping is one-to-one. | `REQ-013` | A rejection identifies failed criteria, evidence, and required changes, distinguishing mandatory defects from optional improvements., The originating solver returns a new candidate version and a response to findings. | `REQ-014` | Any missing, rejected, blocked, or stale review prevents synthesis. A pass on an earlier version does not admit a changed candidate., The synthesis input set corresponds exactly to the eligible reviewed versions. | `satisfied` | 2 | None |

| `REQ-016` | The manager records acceptance of the exact current proposal, requests a bounded correction, or records a specific blocker., The senior cannot authorize implementation, change the user's scope, or close the Task.
